gen-gf-headland-one-gf-lexend-mega: Refined, with a tall-bowled a and e: that's Headland One. Lexend Mega, a sans-serif drawn as if with one nib, keeps its lowercase close to capital height, a sturdy counterweight to the heading's slight modulation.
gen-gf-headland-one-gf-lexend-peta: Headland One is best at refined, classic character, with a middling spread of stroke weight. Lexend Peta is best at wide, unthinned curves and a big x-height, with no modulation at all.
gen-gf-headland-one-gf-lexend-tera: Letters stand as far apart as stepping stones, each drawn in a single plotter-pen line. Lexend Tera is the sans-serif doing that, while Headland One earns its keep large and brief, where its gentle stroke variation shows.
gen-gf-headland-one-gf-lexend-zetta: Widely tracked letters, tall in the body, sit under Headland One. Lexend Zetta, a sans-serif of constant-width strokes, would read steadily across many lines, its spacing giving each word room.
gen-gf-headland-one-gf-montserrat-altern: Montserrat Alternates has chalk-board lowercase that crowds toward the capital line, its curves as stout as the stems. Under Headland One, a long run of it feels dense and cord-like.
gen-gf-hedvig-letters-serif-gf-cascadia-: Cascadia Code spaces its letters out where you can't miss it. Its wire-like monoline strokes meet the dip-pen modulation of Hedvig Letters Serif, so a slightly smaller body size would let that big lowercase eye lead.
Cascadia Mono stands its letters like pins in a wide board, curves matching the stems. And Hedvig Letters Serif, with its dip-pen shading, lends an editorial voice the body never tries to supply.
gen-gf-hedvig-letters-serif-gf-julius-sa: Hedvig Letters Serif has bowls like a cupped palm of clay and an oversized lowercase eye. Julius Sans One's drafting-pen outlines, all one nib width, are what stand out.
gen-gf-hedvig-letters-serif-gf-lexend-ex: Editorial in feel, Hedvig Letters Serif lets light strokes recede only slightly. Lexend Exa has unshaded, constant strokes and a big x-height, which would crowd the heading if the body were made large.
gen-gf-hedvig-letters-serif-gf-lexend-gi: An outsized eye in the lowercase defines Hedvig Letters Serif, with soft accents of heavier stroke. Lexend Giga, a sans-serif of flat single-weight lines and generous tracking, sits next to it like a level, open-handed counterpart.
